title: OpenAI Lines Up Google's TPUs While Nvidia Backs Its $500B Ohio Lease
subhead: Two stories on the same day show the AI compute market loosening Nvidia's grip on silicon even as Nvidia tightens its grip on the balance sheets: OpenAI is reportedly buying Google TPUs, and Nvidia is expected to guarantee a 10-gigawatt Ohio campus lease valued at $500 billion.

sections.heading: Google's TPUs Land Oracle, With OpenAI Reportedly Next
sections.body:
Google's Tensor Processing Units gained one confirmed and one reported major customer within a week, per DigiTimes. Oracle is the confirmed buyer; OpenAI is the reported one. Reuters, citing a report by The Information, said OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, with financial terms undisclosed. Google and OpenAI did not comment publicly.

OpenAI is one of Nvidia's largest GPU buyers. Reuters reported in June 2025 that OpenAI had begun renting Google chips; a purchase would be a step beyond that. Google began selling TPUs directly to some external customers this year, and the seventh-generation Ironwood TPU has been marketed by Google as designed for inference at production scale.

The commercial logic is straightforward: TPUs are positioned as a cheaper alternative to Nvidia for running, not just training, models. DigiTimes frames the Oracle and OpenAI deals as adding pressure on Nvidia, whose GPUs still dominate the market.
sections.whyItMatters: A second viable accelerator supply at scale changes the negotiating position of every large AI buyer — and gives Google a hardware business that does not depend on its own models winning.

sections.heading: Nvidia Moves From Supplier to Lease Guarantor on a 10-Gigawatt Ohio Site
sections.body:
OpenAI is in advanced talks to lease a proposed 10-gigawatt data center campus in southern Ohio, Network World reports, citing The Information. The build could cost at least $500 billion at current prices for chips, power and construction. OpenAI would control the computing equipment under a 20-year lease and begin payments once the site operates, with a first phase expected in 2028. Nvidia is expected to supply hardware and guarantee both OpenAI's lease obligations and the developer's financing.

The site aligns with a Department of Energy project announced in March to redevelop the former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant near Piketon, Ohio. SB Energy, a SoftBank Group company, committed to building 10 gigawatts of new generation there — at least 9.2 gigawatts of it natural gas — plus transmission. The DOE did not name a tenant at the time.

This extends a September 2025 OpenAI-Nvidia partnership to deploy at least 10 gigawatts of Nvidia systems, under which Nvidia said it intended to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI as each gigawatt came online. Separately, DigiTimes reports SpaceX turned Nvidia GPUs into long-duration assets via a $40 billion Apollo deal — another sign that GPU fleets are being financed like infrastructure rather than bought like equipment.
sections.whyItMatters: When a chip supplier guarantees its customer's lease and the developer's financing, the vendor-customer line disappears. Analysts quoted by Network World put it plainly: the relationship becomes sponsor and tenant. Enterprises standardizing on OpenAI are then exposed to one company spanning silicon, power and capital.

sections.heading: AMD Pays Meta $1 Billion for the Right to Be Second Source
sections.body:
AMD said on October 27 that it will invest $1 billion in Meta's stock sale as its Helios racks enter testing, according to DigiTimes, which describes AMD as backing one of its largest AI customers with capital and chips.

The pattern matches Nvidia's Ohio structure in miniature: accelerator vendors are now putting equity or credit behind the buyers of their hardware to lock in demand years ahead of delivery.
sections.whyItMatters: The compute buildout is being financed by the companies selling the compute. That keeps orders flowing but concentrates risk — if AI demand cools, the same vendors hold the lease guarantees and the equity stakes.

sections.heading: Sydney Says AI Has Rewritten the Cyber Threat Timeline
sections.body:
The Australian Signals Directorate warned Tuesday that AI poses an 'unprecedented' threat to networks and critical infrastructure, per Yeni Safak and MSN reporting on the annual cyber threat report. The ASD said it issued more than 4,400 warnings about potentially malicious activity over the past year — an 80 percent increase on the prior 12 months — and that AI was the defining force in the threat landscape.

The report flagged 'new threats from the unintended actions of AI agents and model testing,' and attributed activity against Australian organisations to actors linked to China, Russia and North Korea, targeting government networks, critical infrastructure, private business and individuals.

Defence Minister Richard Marles said AI 'is here and it's real,' and urged Australians to update and harden systems. The warning landed as governments and firms scrambled to fix flaws in a widely used programming language after a vulnerability was found using a powerful OpenAI model, per the same reporting.
sections.whyItMatters: The 80 percent jump in warning volume is an operational signal, not a rhetorical one: AI is compressing the interval between a vulnerability being disclosed and being exploited. Defensive timelines set on human-paced patching no longer hold.

sections.heading: Brussels Grants Silicon Box's Novara Plant Foundry Status Under the Chips Act
sections.body:
The European Commission granted Open EU Foundry status to Silicon Box's facility in Novara, Italy under the European Chips Act, per mybusiness.com. The designation brings administrative support, faster approvals and priority access to Chips for Europe pilot lines, with part of capacity reserved for external customers. Italy approved a $3.7 billion package for the plant.

Crucially, Novara is advanced packaging and testing, not wafer fabrication — using panel-level packaging to integrate multiple chiplets into a single package. The plant is expected to reach full capacity by 2033. The Commission says it has approved projects totaling more than €31.5 billion in combined public and private investment, against a target of doubling Europe's global chip market share to 20 percent by 2030.
sections.whyItMatters: Europe's clearest semiconductor win this week is downstream of the fab. Packaging is where AI accelerators are assembled, and it has been concentrated in Taiwan and Southeast Asia. Capacity there is strategic in a way a mature-node fab is not.

sections.heading: Starlink Passes 10,000 Satellites; Rivals Are Still Counting in Hundreds
sections.body:
More than 10,000 active Starlink satellites are now in orbit — roughly two-thirds of all satellites around Earth — according to tracking by astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell, as reported by Scientific American. SpaceX has launched 11,529 Starlink satellites since May 2019, with the remainder being replacements for deorbited units.

The nearest operational competitor, Europe's OneWeb, has 654 satellites. Amazon's Leo constellation has launched about 200 of more than 7,500 planned. China's state-backed Qianfan and Guowang constellations target 15,000 and 13,000 respectively, with Qianfan at roughly 200 satellites as of late 2025 and an approved ramp toward 15,000.

In Taiwan, FarEasTone signed an agreement on October 27 with direct-to-device provider Elveo Mobile to expand satellite-to-phone service, DigiTimes reports — a reminder that the ground segment is where second-tier operators are competing.
sections.whyItMatters: The gap is now so large that it is a policy problem rather than a market outcome. Starlink's position in Ukraine has already made the question of who can switch a network off a live diplomatic issue; 10,000 satellites makes that question structural.

bottomLine: The AI hardware market moved in two directions at once on Tuesday. Google's TPUs signed Oracle and are reportedly heading to OpenAI, which at last gives buyers an alternative to Nvidia at scale. But Nvidia is responding by becoming the financier of its customers rather than just their supplier — expected to guarantee a 20-year lease on a $500 billion, 10-gigawatt Ohio campus, and already tied into a $40 billion SpaceX financing arrangement. AMD is doing the same with a $1 billion stake in Meta. Compute orders are being secured with vendor balance sheets, which works while demand rises and becomes uncomfortable if it stalls. Elsewhere, Australia's 80 percent surge in cyber warnings shows AI cutting the time between vulnerability and exploitation; Europe's Chips Act added advanced packaging capacity in Italy, the segment that matters most for AI chips; and Starlink passed 10,000 satellites, two-thirds of everything in orbit.
sources: DigiTimes, Reuters via Economic Times, Network World, Scientific American, Yeni Safak, MSN, mybusiness.com, CEPA (analysis), Jonathan McDowell's space statistics
